Build a relatedness network from kinship estimates

Source: R/rkn_graph_from_kinship.R
rkn_graph_from_kinship.Rd

Builds the relatedness network used by rkn_select_random, rkn_select_criteria, rkn_select_global and rkn_tradeoff: one vertex per sample, and an edge between two samples whose kinship coefficient is at least threshold. The families of the selectors are the connected components of this network.

Usage

rkn_graph_from_kinship(
  x,
  threshold,
  samples = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  covariates_id = "id",
  check = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

Kinship estimates, either a square symmetric matrix with the sample identifiers as row and column names (the diagonal is ignored), or a data frame with one row per pair of samples, such as the .kin0 output of KING or the output of plink2 --make-king-table. In a data frame, the two identifier columns are recognised by the names ID1 and ID2 (KING), IID1 and IID2 (PLINK 2) or id1 and id2, and the kinship column by the name kinship, regardless of case.

threshold

The kinship coefficient from which two samples are considered related: a number, or one of "duplicate", "first", "second" and "third", which select the cutoff of KING for relatives of that degree or closer (see Details). There is no default: the choice depends on the study.

samples

Optional character vector with the identifiers of all genotyped samples, for instance the IID column of the PLINK .fam or .psam file. Pair tables usually list only related pairs, so samples without relatives appear in no row; samples adds them to the network as unrelated individuals. Ignored for a matrix.

exclude

Optional character vector of sample identifiers to leave out of the network, for instance samples flagged by a quality check.

covariates

Optional data frame of sample covariates, with the sample identifiers in the column named by covariates_id. Its other columns become vertex attributes of the network, which rkn_select_criteria and rkn_select_global read; samples missing from covariates get NA. Covariates cannot be named name, which holds the sample identifiers, nor degree, max_path_length or .name, which are reserved for the structural measures computed during the selection.

covariates_id

Name of the identifier column of covariates.

check

Logical. If TRUE (default), the samples left after exclude are checked with rkn_check_samples, with the same threshold and default settings, and a single warning summarises the possible duplicates and contamination it finds. Nothing is removed. Samples of possibly different ancestry, which do not affect the selection, are reported only by rkn_check_samples(). check = FALSE skips the check, for instance when rebuilding a network whose samples were already checked.

Value

An undirected igraph object with one vertex per sample: the vertex attribute name holds the sample identifiers and the other vertex attributes the covariates, the edge attribute kinship holds the kinship coefficient, and the graph attribute kinship_threshold holds the cutoff used.

Details

The threshold labels select the boundaries between the degrees of relationship inferred by KING (Manichaikul et al., 2010):

labelcutoffrelatives joined, for instance
"duplicate"0.354the same individual genotyped twice, monozygotic twins
"first"0.177parent and child, full siblings, and the above
"second"0.0884grandparent and grandchild, aunt or uncle and nephew or niece, half-siblings, and the above
"third"0.0442first cousins, and the above

Pairs with a missing kinship estimate are treated as unrelated, with a warning.

The sample check runs here, rather than in the selectors, because it needs the kinship of every pair of samples, including the unrelated ones, which the network no longer holds. A network built in another way can be checked by calling rkn_check_samples on the kinship estimates it was built from.

References

Manichaikul A, Mychaleckyj JC, Rich SS, Daly K, Sale M, Chen WM (2010). Robust relationship inference in genome-wide association studies. Bioinformatics, 26(22), 2867–2873. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btq559

See also

rkn_check_samples, rkn_select_random, rkn_select_criteria, rkn_select_global, rkn_plot_pre.

Examples

# Kinship estimates for six samples: a parent and child (A, B), first cousins (C, D)
# and two unrelated samples (E, F).
K <- matrix(-0.01, 6, 6, dimnames = list(LETTERS[1:6], LETTERS[1:6]))
K["A", "B"] <- K["B", "A"] <- 0.25
K["C", "D"] <- K["D", "C"] <- 0.06
diag(K) <- 0.5

# Relatives of the third degree or closer: two families of two, two singletons
g <- rkn_graph_from_kinship(K, threshold = "third")
igraph::components(g)$csize
#> [1] 2 2 1 1

# First-degree relatives only: the cousins count as unrelated
igraph::components(rkn_graph_from_kinship(K, threshold = "first"))$csize
#> [1] 2 1 1 1 1

# The same data as a pair table that lists only the related pairs, as KING does;
# samples adds the unrelated E and F
pairs <- data.frame(ID1 = c("A", "C"), ID2 = c("B", "D"), Kinship = c(0.25, 0.06))
g <- rkn_graph_from_kinship(pairs, threshold = "third", samples = LETTERS[1:6])

# Covariates for a criteria-based selection
covariates <- data.frame(id = LETTERS[1:6], sex = c("M", "F", "F", "M", "M", "F"))
g <- rkn_graph_from_kinship(K, threshold = "third", covariates = covariates)
rkn_select_criteria(g, rkn_criterion_level("sex", "F"), seed = 1)$kept
#> [1] "B" "C" "E" "F"
